title: EVAP System Purge Control Valve "B" Performance/Stuck Open
plain: The purge valve lets fuel vapor from the charcoal canister into the engine to be burned. The computer thinks the second ("B") purge valve isn't working right or is stuck open.
symptoms: Check engine light
Hard to start right after filling the tank
Rough idle for a short time after refueling

causes.name: Purge valve stuck open
Wiring or connector problem at the valve
Software problem that an update may fix

checks: Check whether the purge valve holds vacuum when it's off
Check the valve's wiring and connector
Ask the dealer about bulletins or software updates (the Bulletins page explains what a bulletin is)
fix: Usually a new purge valve, or a software update if the carmaker has one.

title: Crankcase Ventilation System Disconnected
plain: The computer thinks a crankcase vent (PCV) hose has come off or is cracked, so oily vapor from inside the engine may be escaping.
symptoms: Check engine light, sometimes coming back after it's cleared
Hissing sound or rough idle on some engines
Oil smell from the engine bay on some engines

causes.name: Loose, cracked or disconnected PCV hose
Faulty PCV valve or oil separator
Crankcase pressure sensor fault
Software problem that an update may fix

checks: Look over the PCV hoses for cracks or loose ends
Check the oil fill cap and dipstick are seated
Ask the dealer about bulletins or software updates (the Bulletins page explains what a bulletin is)
fix: Reconnect or replace the PCV hose or valve, or install a software update if the carmaker has one.

title: Cold Start Fuel Pressure Performance Bank 1
plain: When the engine is cold, fuel pressure isn't reaching the level the computer expects during startup and warm-up.
symptoms: Check engine light
Hesitation or stumble while the engine warms up
Hard start when cold

causes.name: Weak high-pressure fuel pump (direct-injection engines)
Weak in-tank fuel pump or clogged fuel filter
Fuel pressure sensor fault
Software problem that an update may fix

checks: Read fuel pressure in live data during a cold start
Check for other fuel pressure codes
Ask the dealer about bulletins or software updates (the Bulletins page explains what a bulletin is)
fix: Depends on the test results: often a software update, a fuel pressure sensor or a fuel pump.

title: Active Grill Air Shutter "A" Position Sensor Circuit
plain: Many newer cars have shutters behind the front grille that open and close to help fuel economy and engine warm-up. The computer sees a problem with the sensor that reports the shutter position.
symptoms: Check engine light
Grille shutters may stay open or closed

causes.name: Shutter motor or sensor fault
Wiring or connector problem behind the bumper
Shutters blocked by ice, snow or road debris

checks: Look for ice, debris or damage in the grille shutters
Check the shutter connector and wiring
Command the shutters open and closed with a scan tool
fix: Usually a new shutter motor or wiring repair.
drive: It usually doesn't change how the car drives. If the shutters are stuck closed, the engine can run warm in heat or when towing, so watch the temperature gauge; if it climbs toward H or you see steam, pull over and turn the engine off.

title: Active Grill Air Shutter "A" Stuck On
plain: The grille shutters behind the front grille seem stuck in one position and aren't moving when the computer tells them to.
symptoms: Check engine light
Grille shutters stuck open or closed

causes.name: Shutters frozen or jammed by ice, snow or debris
Failed shutter motor
Broken shutter linkage
Wiring problem

checks: Look for ice, debris or damage in the grille shutters
Command the shutters with a scan tool and watch them move
Check the shutter motor connector
fix: Clear the jam, or replace the shutter motor or shutter assembly.
drive: It usually doesn't change how the car drives. If the shutters are stuck closed, the engine can run warm in heat or when towing, so watch the temperature gauge; if it climbs toward H or you see steam, pull over and turn the engine off.

title: Engine Oil Pressure Control Circuit/Open
plain: Some engines have an oil pump that can change its pressure. The engine computer controls it with a solenoid or valve, and it sees an open or broken circuit to that control.
symptoms: Check engine light
Oil pressure warning on some vehicles
Engine usually runs normally

causes.name: Wiring or connector problem at the oil pressure control solenoid
Failed oil pressure control solenoid
Low oil level
Engine computer fault (rare)

checks: Check the oil level and that the right oil grade is in the engine
Check the solenoid's connector and wiring for damage or oil inside
Confirm real oil pressure with a mechanical gauge
fix: Usually a wiring repair or a new oil pressure control solenoid.
drive: Check the oil level as soon as you can safely stop. If the oil is low or you hear ticking or knocking, turn the engine off and don't drive it. If the oil is full and the engine sounds normal, get it checked soon.
test_first: Check the oil level and confirm real oil pressure with a mechanical gauge before replacing parts. Low pressure points to the pump, pickup or bearings, not just the solenoid.

title: Engine Oil Pressure Control Circuit Performance/Stuck Off
plain: The engine computer told the variable oil pump to change pressure, but the oil pressure didn't change the way it expected. The control may be stuck.
symptoms: Check engine light
Oil pressure warning on some vehicles
Engine may tick or sound louder on some engines

causes.name: Low oil level or wrong oil grade
Sticking or failed oil pressure control solenoid
Clogged oil filter or oil pickup screen
Worn oil pump
Faulty oil pressure sensor

checks: Check the oil level and that the right oil grade is in the engine
Confirm real oil pressure with a mechanical gauge
Command the solenoid with a scan tool and watch the oil pressure change
fix: Depends on the test: an oil change, a new solenoid or sensor, or oil pump repair.
drive: Check the oil level as soon as you can safely stop. If the oil is low or you hear ticking or knocking, turn the engine off and don't drive it. If the oil is full and the engine sounds normal, get it checked soon.
test_first: Check the oil level and confirm real oil pressure with a mechanical gauge before replacing parts. Low pressure points to the pump, pickup or bearings, not just the solenoid.

title: Engine Failed to Start
plain: In a hybrid, the computer tried to start the gas engine and it didn't start. The car may move on battery power for a short time and then stop.
symptoms: Check engine and hybrid warning lights
Gas engine doesn't start when it should
Car may lose power after a short distance on battery power

causes.name: Out of gas or very low fuel
Ignition problem such as a bad coil or plugs
Fuel delivery problem such as a weak fuel pump
Crankshaft or camshaft sensor problem
Hybrid starting system or software fault

checks: Make sure there is gas in the tank (refill if the gauge is near empty)
Read all engine and hybrid codes, since another code often shows the real cause
Check fuel pressure, spark and engine sensor signals while the hybrid system tries to start the engine
Ask the dealer about software updates, bulletins and warranty coverage for the hybrid system (the Bulletins page explains what a bulletin is)
fix: Fix the cause of the no-start, which is often fuel, spark or a sensor. Running out of gas is a common cause in hybrids.
drive: Check the fuel gauge first; if it's near empty, add fuel. Otherwise drive only as far as needed to get somewhere safe, because the car may run out of battery power and stop. Get it checked soon.
test_first: Hybrid and EV systems use dangerous high voltage. Only a trained technician should test the battery pack, orange cables or inverter. A shop should read all hybrid codes and battery data before replacing the battery, since a fan, sensor, connection or software update can set the same code.
urgent_if: If the car suddenly loses power, won't speed up, or a red hybrid or EV system warning tells you to stop, turn on your hazards, move right and get off the road when it's safe. Put it in Park and turn it off. Don't keep driving in traffic; have it towed.

title: Battery Energy Control Module
plain: The computer that watches the high-voltage hybrid or EV battery has found a problem with itself or its signals.
symptoms: Hybrid system or EV warning light, often with the check engine light
Less power, or the gas engine runs more than normal
Worse fuel economy or shorter electric range
Car may not go into Ready mode

causes.name: Battery control module fault or water damage
Loose or corroded connector at the module
Weak 12-volt battery causing low voltage
Software problem that an update may fix

checks: Test the 12-volt battery, since low voltage can upset hybrid computers
Read all hybrid codes and battery data with a scan tool
Check the module's power, ground and connectors
Ask the dealer about software updates, bulletins and warranty coverage for the hybrid system (the Bulletins page explains what a bulletin is)
fix: Usually a connector or wiring repair, a software update, or a new battery control module, once a technician confirms it.
drive: The car may limit power or run the gas engine more than normal to protect the battery. Drive gently, stay off highways if power feels low, and get it checked soon by a shop that works on hybrids or EVs. Ask whether the hybrid battery warranty may cover it.
test_first: Hybrid and EV systems use dangerous high voltage. Only a trained technician should test the battery pack, orange cables or inverter. A shop should read all hybrid codes and battery data before replacing the battery, since a fan, sensor, connection or software update can set the same code.
urgent_if: If the car suddenly loses power, won't speed up, or a red hybrid or EV system warning tells you to stop, turn on your hazards, move right and get off the road when it's safe. Put it in Park and turn it off. Don't keep driving in traffic; have it towed.

title: Drive Motor "A" Over Temperature
plain: The electric drive motor is getting too hot. The car usually cuts power to protect it.
symptoms: Hybrid or EV warning, or a 'power is limited' message
Car speeds up weakly or won't go fast
May happen more in hot weather, on hills or when towing

causes.name: Low coolant in the motor or inverter cooling system
Failed electric coolant pump
Blocked radiator or cooling fan problem
Faulty motor temperature sensor
Hard driving, steep hills or towing in heat

checks: With everything cold, check the motor/inverter coolant level (it is often a separate reservoir)
Check that the electric coolant pump runs
Compare the motor temperature reading with real temperature
Ask the dealer about software updates, bulletins and warranty coverage for the hybrid system (the Bulletins page explains what a bulletin is)
fix: Fix the cooling problem, often a coolant leak or a failed electric coolant pump; a damaged motor may need replacing.
drive: Let the car cool down before driving on, and drive gently. Never open a radiator or coolant cap while the engine or motor is hot; it can spray scalding coolant. Get it checked soon by a shop that works on hybrids or EVs.
test_first: Hybrid and EV systems use dangerous high voltage. Only a trained technician should test the battery pack, orange cables or inverter. A shop should read all hybrid codes and battery data before replacing the battery, since a fan, sensor, connection or software update can set the same code.
urgent_if: If the car suddenly loses power, won't speed up, or a red hybrid or EV system warning tells you to stop, turn on your hazards, move right and get off the road when it's safe. Put it in Park and turn it off. Don't keep driving in traffic; have it towed.

title: Drive Motor "A" Inverter Over Temperature
plain: The inverter, the box of electronics that powers the electric drive motor, is getting too hot. The car usually cuts power to protect it.
symptoms: Hybrid or EV warning, or a powertrain over-temperature message
Less power or the car won't go fast
Coolant warning on some vehicles

causes.name: Low coolant in the inverter cooling system
Failed electric inverter coolant pump
Blocked radiator or cooling fan problem
Faulty inverter temperature sensor
Inverter fault

checks: With everything cold, check the inverter coolant level
Check that the inverter coolant pump runs
Look for coolant leaks around the inverter and hoses
Ask the dealer about software updates, bulletins and warranty coverage for the hybrid system (the Bulletins page explains what a bulletin is)
fix: Fix the cooling problem, often low coolant or a failed coolant pump; sometimes the inverter itself needs replacing.
drive: Let the car cool down before driving on, and drive gently. Never open a radiator or coolant cap while the engine or motor is hot; it can spray scalding coolant. Get it checked soon by a shop that works on hybrids or EVs.
test_first: Hybrid and EV systems use dangerous high voltage. Only a trained technician should test the battery pack, orange cables or inverter. A shop should read all hybrid codes and battery data before replacing the battery, since a fan, sensor, connection or software update can set the same code.
urgent_if: If the car suddenly loses power, won't speed up, or a red hybrid or EV system warning tells you to stop, turn on your hazards, move right and get off the road when it's safe. Put it in Park and turn it off. Don't keep driving in traffic; have it towed.

title: Generator Inverter Performance
plain: The inverter that controls the hybrid's generator motor isn't working the way the computer expects.
symptoms: Hybrid system or EV warning light, often with the check engine light
Less power, or the gas engine runs more than normal
Worse fuel economy or shorter electric range

causes.name: Inverter fault
Inverter cooling problem such as a failed coolant pump
Loose or corroded high-voltage connection
Software problem that an update may fix

checks: Read all hybrid codes and freeze-frame data
Check the inverter coolant level and pump (everything cold)
Have a trained technician test the inverter
Ask the dealer about software updates, bulletins and warranty coverage for the hybrid system (the Bulletins page explains what a bulletin is)
fix: Often a software update or a new inverter, depending on what the technician finds.
drive: The car may limit power or run the gas engine more than normal to protect the battery. Drive gently, stay off highways if power feels low, and get it checked soon by a shop that works on hybrids or EVs. Ask whether the hybrid battery warranty may cover it.
test_first: Hybrid and EV systems use dangerous high voltage. Only a trained technician should test the battery pack, orange cables or inverter. A shop should read all hybrid codes and battery data before replacing the battery, since a fan, sensor, connection or software update can set the same code.

title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack State of Charge Low
plain: The high-voltage battery's charge has dropped too low. This can happen if the car sat unused for a long time, ran out of gas, or a part isn't charging the battery.
symptoms: Hybrid or EV warning light
Car may not start or go into Ready mode
Little power, or auto start-stop stops working (mild hybrids)

causes.name: Car sat unused for weeks, or was left in Ready or Neutral for a long time
Ran out of gas (hybrids)
Weak or worn high-voltage battery
Charging system or battery control fault

checks: Make sure there's gas in the tank
Read the battery state of charge and cell data with a scan tool
Have the shop recharge the battery and retest
Ask the dealer about software updates, bulletins and warranty coverage for the hybrid system (the Bulletins page explains what a bulletin is)
fix: Often recharging the battery and fixing whatever drained it; a worn battery may need replacing.
drive: The car may limit power or run the gas engine more than normal to protect the battery. Drive gently, stay off highways if power feels low, and get it checked soon by a shop that works on hybrids or EVs. Ask whether the hybrid battery warranty may cover it.
test_first: Hybrid and EV systems use dangerous high voltage. Only a trained technician should test the battery pack, orange cables or inverter. A shop should read all hybrid codes and battery data before replacing the battery, since a fan, sensor, connection or software update can set the same code.
urgent_if: If the car suddenly loses power, won't speed up, or a red hybrid or EV system warning tells you to stop, turn on your hazards, move right and get off the road when it's safe. Put it in Park and turn it off. Don't keep driving in traffic; have it towed.

title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Deterioration
plain: The computer has found that the high-voltage battery can't store or deliver as much energy as it should. It is losing capacity as it wears.
symptoms: Hybrid system or EV warning light, often with the check engine light
Less power, or the gas engine runs more than normal
Worse fuel economy or shorter electric range
Battery gauge drops or fills very fast

causes.name: Worn hybrid battery
Dirty or blocked battery cooling fan or vent
Uneven or weak battery sections
Battery control software that an update may fix

checks: Check that the battery cooling vent (often near a rear seat) isn't blocked by bags, dust or pet hair
Read battery section voltages and temperatures with a scan tool
Ask the dealer about software updates, bulletins and warranty coverage for the hybrid system (the Bulletins page explains what a bulletin is)
fix: Often a software update, a cleaned cooling fan, or a rebuilt or new hybrid battery, once tests confirm it.
drive: The car may limit power or run the gas engine more than normal to protect the battery. Drive gently, stay off highways if power feels low, and get it checked soon by a shop that works on hybrids or EVs. Ask whether the hybrid battery warranty may cover it.
test_first: Hybrid and EV systems use dangerous high voltage. Only a trained technician should test the battery pack, orange cables or inverter. A shop should read all hybrid codes and battery data before replacing the battery, since a fan, sensor, connection or software update can set the same code.
urgent_if: If the car suddenly loses power, won't speed up, or a red hybrid or EV system warning tells you to stop, turn on your hazards, move right and get off the road when it's safe. Put it in Park and turn it off. Don't keep driving in traffic; have it towed.

title: Replace Hybrid/EV Battery Pack
plain: The computer has found that one or more sections of the high-voltage battery are much weaker than the rest. The battery may be wearing out.
symptoms: Hybrid system or EV warning light, often with the check engine light
Less power, or the gas engine runs more than normal
Worse fuel economy or shorter electric range
Battery gauge swings quickly between low and high

causes.name: Worn hybrid battery sections
Dirty or blocked battery cooling fan or vent
Loose or corroded connections inside the battery pack
Battery sensor or control module fault

checks: Check that the battery cooling vent (often near a rear seat) isn't blocked by bags, dust or pet hair
Read each battery section's voltage with a scan tool to find weak ones
Have the battery tested under load by a hybrid-trained shop
Ask the dealer about software updates, bulletins and warranty coverage for the hybrid system (the Bulletins page explains what a bulletin is)
fix: Usually a rebuilt or new hybrid battery, or replacing weak sections; sometimes a cleaned cooling fan or new connections.
drive: The car may limit power or run the gas engine more than normal to protect the battery. Drive gently, stay off highways if power feels low, and get it checked soon by a shop that works on hybrids or EVs. Ask whether the hybrid battery warranty may cover it.
test_first: Hybrid and EV systems use dangerous high voltage. Only a trained technician should test the battery pack, orange cables or inverter. A shop should read all hybrid codes and battery data before replacing the battery, since a fan, sensor, connection or software update can set the same code.
urgent_if: If the car suddenly loses power, won't speed up, or a red hybrid or EV system warning tells you to stop, turn on your hazards, move right and get off the road when it's safe. Put it in Park and turn it off. Don't keep driving in traffic; have it towed.

title: DC/DC Converter "A" Performance
plain: The DC/DC converter turns high voltage from the hybrid or EV battery into 12 volts to charge the small battery and run the lights and electronics. The computer says it isn't working right.
symptoms: Hybrid or EV warning, sometimes the battery (charging) light
12-volt battery runs down
Lights dim or electronics act up; the car may shut down if the 12-volt battery gets too low

causes.name: DC/DC converter fault
Converter cooling problem
Blown fuse or bad connection to the 12-volt battery
Weak 12-volt battery

checks: Test the 12-volt battery and its connections
Measure 12-volt system voltage with the car in Ready mode
Check the converter's fuses, connectors and coolant
Ask the dealer about software updates, bulletins and warranty coverage for the hybrid system (the Bulletins page explains what a bulletin is)
fix: Often a new DC/DC converter (sometimes built into the inverter), or a fuse, connection or 12-volt battery.
drive: Turn off extras like heated seats and the stereo and head straight to a shop. The 12-volt battery may be draining, so the car could shut down or not restart. Don't turn it off away from home if you can avoid it.
test_first: Hybrid and EV systems use dangerous high voltage. Only a trained technician should test the battery pack, orange cables or inverter. A shop should read all hybrid codes and battery data before replacing the battery, since a fan, sensor, connection or software update can set the same code.
urgent_if: If the car suddenly loses power, won't speed up, or a red hybrid or EV system warning tells you to stop, turn on your hazards, move right and get off the road when it's safe. Put it in Park and turn it off. Don't keep driving in traffic; have it towed.

title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage System Isolation Fault
plain: The computer has found high voltage leaking from the hybrid or EV system to the car's metal body. This is a safety fault, so the car may shut down the high-voltage system.
symptoms: Hybrid or EV warning message
Car may not go into Ready mode, or may lose drive power
Sometimes appears after rain, a car wash or a flood

causes.name: Water or coolant getting into a high-voltage part or connector
Damaged insulation on an orange high-voltage cable
Electric A/C compressor or heater fault
Battery pack or inverter fault

checks: Have a trained technician run an insulation test on each high-voltage part
Check for coolant leaks into the inverter or battery
Check the VIN for open recalls
Ask the dealer about software updates, bulletins and warranty coverage for the hybrid system (the Bulletins page explains what a bulletin is)
fix: Find and fix the high-voltage part that is leaking voltage, which may be a cable, compressor, inverter or the battery itself.
drive: Have it towed to a shop or dealer trained on high-voltage systems. Don't touch orange cables or open the battery pack. If you see smoke or smell burning plastic, get everyone out, move well away from the car and call 911.
test_first: Hybrid and EV systems use dangerous high voltage. Only a trained technician should test the battery pack, orange cables or inverter. A shop should read all hybrid codes and battery data before replacing the battery, since a fan, sensor, connection or software update can set the same code.
urgent_if: If the car suddenly loses power, won't speed up, or a red hybrid or EV system warning tells you to stop, turn on your hazards, move right and get off the road when it's safe. Put it in Park and turn it off. Don't keep driving in traffic; have it towed.

title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump "A" Motor Current Low
plain: Many hybrids and cars with auto start-stop use a small electric pump to keep transmission fluid pressure up while the engine is off. The computer sees too little electric current in that pump's motor.
symptoms: Check engine light
Auto start-stop or electric drive may stop working
Delay, slip or clunk when pulling away after a stop

causes.name: Failed auxiliary transmission fluid pump
Wiring or connector problem at the pump
Low transmission fluid
Blown fuse or relay

checks: Check the transmission fluid level the way the owner's manual says
Check the pump's fuse, connector and wiring
Command the pump on with a scan tool and measure its current
fix: Usually a new auxiliary pump or a wiring repair.
drive: If the car hesitates, slips or won't move after an auto-stop, turn auto start-stop off if your car allows it and get it checked soon. If it won't move at all, put it in Park, turn on your hazards and call for a tow.

title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump "A" Motor Current High
plain: Many hybrids and cars with auto start-stop use a small electric pump to keep transmission fluid pressure up while the engine is off. The computer sees too much electric current in that pump's motor.
symptoms: Check engine light
Auto start-stop or electric drive may stop working
Delay, slip or clunk when pulling away after a stop

causes.name: Failed or binding auxiliary transmission fluid pump
Short in the pump wiring
Low or dirty transmission fluid making the pump work hard
Control module fault

checks: Check the transmission fluid level the way the owner's manual says
Check the pump's fuse, connector and wiring
Command the pump on with a scan tool and measure its current
fix: Usually a new auxiliary pump or a wiring repair.
drive: If the car hesitates, slips or won't move after an auto-stop, turn auto start-stop off if your car allows it and get it checked soon. If it won't move at all, put it in Park, turn on your hazards and call for a tow.
